questions.question: On the break-even map, what do the x and y axes show?
options: x is q (preferred close over $100 notional), y is m (net mNAV)
x is the coin price, y is the share price
x is the week, y is n
x is dollars moved, y is value to common
questions.explanation: Each mark is one firm-week at (q, m). The diagonal m = q is where both rotations add nothing.

questions.question: Which chart library does the page load?
options: D3 from a CDN
Chart.js from jsDelivr
Plotly
None: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with hand-drawn SVG
questions.explanation: Decision M6: no external scripts or styles. index.html loads only style.css and app.js.

questions.question: The mapped values run from m = 0.7222 to m = 1.4212. Using the page's rule (min − 0.05 and max + 0.05, rounded out to 0.05), what is the shared domain?
questions.explanation: floor((0.7222 − 0.05) × 20) / 20 = 0.65 and ceil((1.4212 + 0.05) × 20) / 20 = 1.50. Both axes use it, so m = q is a true diagonal.

questions.question: Strategy's week ending 2026-08-23 has a price part of +$4,328.6M and an issue common part of −$215.2M. Why are price moves left out of the stacked bars?
options: Price moves are estimates
Price moves are not in attribution.csv
The price part is often 10 to 50 times a week's actions and would hide them; it stays in the tooltip and table
The page only shows negative values
questions.explanation: Decision M8. At this week's scale the actions would be a sliver next to the price bar. The price part stays in the tooltip, the totals strip and the table.

questions.question: In the week ending 2026-10-04, Strategy's net mNAV is 1.199212 and STRC closed at $99.41. What does the by-week panel plot for that week?
options: $99.41 on a dollar scale of its own
99.41 ÷ 119.92 = 83% of break-even, on the same percent scale as BitMine and SharpLink
1.199, the net mNAV
$20.51, the gap to break-even
questions.explanation: Break-even is $100 × m = $119.92. The panel plots the close as a percent of break-even, q ÷ m × 100, on one scale shared by all three firms. Dollars move into the point's tooltip.

questions.question: Why do the attribution bars use basis points of that week's n instead of dollars of value to common?
options: Basis points are easier to compute
Dollars are not in data.json
One bp scale can be shared by firms of different size; on a dollar scale SharpLink's bars would not show next to Strategy's, so each firm would need its own scale
The framing rules ban dollar figures
questions.explanation: bp = value to common ÷ (n × S × p) × 10,000 = Δn ÷ n × 10,000. Strategy's net coin value is about 34 times SharpLink's. Dollars stay in the tooltip, the strips and the table.

questions.question: In PR #7's headless Chromium check, what shows there is no horizontal scroll at 375px?
options: w and sw are both 375: the scroll width equals the viewport width
dots is 33
tabstops0 is 2
arrowMoves is true
questions.explanation: sw is the document's scroll width. When it equals the viewport width w, nothing overflows sideways.

questions.question: The filed 7/26 STRC retirement added $3.893M to common, 0.011% of Strategy's net coin value that week. Why does the mechanism section draw a toy balance sheet instead?
options: The filed figures are estimates
At true scale the trade would not show; a toy with labeled numbers draws the mechanism and the text gives the real share
Toy numbers make the effect look larger than it is
The 8-K does not state the price paid
questions.explanation: Drawing the real trade bigger than its scale would raise the Lie Factor. The toy is labeled "Illustration, not filed figures", and the filed trade follows in words with its 8-K link.
